newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Military, EDS in $35 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel Military, EDS in $35 mln deal.

text.p: Israel Military Industries (IMI) said on Tuesday it has signed a five-year agreement worth $35 million with Electronic Data Systems Corp (EDS) for the outsourcing of its computer unit.

EDS will carry out all of IMI's current computerised activities. The contract comprises a project for converting the information system running on a mainframe in the central computer unit to systems for the company's individual business units.
EDS is committed to employ 80 percent of IMI's computer unit staff.
"This transaction is the first, and moreover innovative, step of its kind in Israel and in the defence industries," IMI chief executive Shlomo Milo said in a statement.
The statement said this was the largest service agreement to date in Israel.
Milo said the agreement was part of the company's organisational and management reorganisation. IMI issued an outsourcing tender in May 1996.
"Outsourcing is now taking its first steps in Israel although the market is ripe for such transactions," Israel Koren, president and chief executive of EDS Israel, said.
